title: How the Rich Pay Less Tax Than You (Legally)
description:
Some of the richest people in America pay a lower tax rate than a nurse or a teacher, and most of the time it's completely legal. In this video I explain how, from three angles: the numbers (capital gains, untaxed growth, buy borrow die, the step up in basis), the psychology of how the wealthy think about taxes, and the legal moves ordinary workers can use this year. Education only, not tax advice.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

15:39 11. Owning, not just earning
16:52 12. Patience pays

18:50 14. Taxes as the biggest bill
20:04 Angle 3: The Playbook
20:25 15. Use pre tax retirement accounts
21:25 16. Use a Roth for tax free growth
22:25 17. The HSA triple advantage
23:39 18. Hold for the long term
24:38 19. Harvest your losses
25:39 20. Build ownership income
26:40 The billionaire and the office
27:41 One worker, three changes
29:24 Tax moves at every age
30:15 Questions people ask
31:52 Tax mistakes that cost regular people
33:16 Recap
33:53 What to do next

Sources:
- IRS: federal income tax brackets, long-term capital gains rates, net investment income tax
- IRS: retirement accounts (401k, IRA, Roth), HSAs, tax-loss harvesting and wash sale rule, qualified charitable distributions
- Social Security Administration: contribution and benefit base (2025 wage limit)
- ProPublica, The Secret IRS Files (June 2021): 3.4% 'true tax rate' for the 25 richest Americans, 2014-2018
- White House CEA and OMB (September 2021): estimated 8.2% average federal individual income tax rate for the 400 wealthiest families
- Warren Buffett, Stop Coddling the Super-Rich (The New York Times, August 14, 2011)
- Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017: three-year holding period for carried interest
- IRS: estate tax basic exclusion amount and step-up in basis rules
- Not tax advice; rules and thresholds change yearly
